questionText:
Read the following case study and answer the question:

"Dr. Radhika, a licensed university psychologist, was providing psychotherapy to Tarun, a 21-year-old engineering student. Tarun was severely distressed following an acrimonious breakup with his classmate, Sneha. During their fourth session, Tarun became intensely agitated, clenched his fists, and stated: 'Sneha betrayed me and humiliated my family. I have purchased an unlicensed firearm and three rounds of ammunition. Tomorrow after our physics lab at 4:00 PM, I am going to shoot her in the parking lot and then end my own life.' Dr. Radhika attempted to de-escalate Tarun, but he abruptly walked out of the clinic. Dr. Radhika faced an urgent ethical and legal dilemma regarding the boundary of client confidentiality versus the preservation of human life."

Which fundamental ethical principle of psychological practice justifies breaching confidentiality to protect an innocent third party?

options.text: Observer Subjectivity
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Beneficence and Non-Maleficence
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Ethics in Psychology.

options.text: Institutional Profit Maximization
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Consumer Autonomy and Hedonism
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Variations in Psychological Attributes (Ethics in Psychology):
Beneficence and Non-Maleficence

Detailed Analysis:
Non-maleficence ('do no harm') and beneficence obligate psychologists to preserve human life; the right of an innocent person to life fundamentally supersedes a client's right to confidentiality.
Hence, Option D is correct.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
